title: The Garden Below
prompt: The walled garden of the first room, but below: the same wall, house, pear tree, stone post, gate, path and sundial in the same places, under a deep violet dusk with no golden sun. Her violet star-lilies fill the raised beds in neat straight rows and nothing else blooms. The stone bench under the tree is straight and clean. A plain wooden swing hangs from a low branch of the pear tree, its ropes tied with a neat bow. The wheelbarrow and the watering can are gone. Everything is perfectly still and tidy: no wind, no fallen leaves, no people, no animals, no writing.
story: Act III: the same garden with only her things in it, and everything too still. Looking registers a difference only when she holds the prologue's claim (the straight bench, no sunflowers, the bow on the swing). Magic works here; each perfecting cast makes it stiller.

variants.fading: the violet star-lilies have half gone grey and bowed over, a few of their petals lie on the path, the swing's rope is frayed; the rest unchanged
variants.dust: a thin grey dust lies over the raised beds, the bench, the swing and the path, and the lantern's light is dimmer; the rest unchanged
